rationale: Under AS9100D clause 8.5.1.2, deviations from design specifications require authorization from the design authority (or delegate) and customer concession where contractually required. The critical signal is buried in the SharePoint delegation matrix: Linda Voss's design authority transferred to James Palmer in March 2026. Palmer's approval is absent from all records, making the lot release non-compliant. Answer B fails because the disposition is not inherently invalid — a proper approval path existed through James Palmer as delegated design authority. The ECN-5429 never being completed is irrelevant to MRB authority (ECNs document changes, not dispositions), and Linda Voss's retirement doesn't create a void because her authority was formally transferred. Answer C fails because Sarah Chen's Quality Manager role allows her to document MRB proceedings and sign the disposition record, but she cannot independently authorize deviation from engineering drawing specifications — that requires the design authority per AS9100D. The audit finding would be: proper design authority (Palmer) was never consulted, revealing a systemic gap between documented procedures and the actual ship-first-document-later practice exposed in the Teams chat.
